request.state: The Can specification derives shell links from authored pages, excluding contextual record/token routes and pages marked nav=none. It supports translated title/group messages, optional order, source-order defaults and deduplicated composition; there is no second menu declaration. Authentication/team context is inherited from data use, an outer require denies a page, and a nested require only gates that region. Ordinary record/action permission checks still run. In the reviewed targets the page registry holds path/render only: CRM sales checks salesperson inside its renderer, and Expense own/review renderers check members and reviewer-or-finance respectively. Those current static-page checks need only canonical identity facts, whereas detail guards inspect records. General pure predicates and page data= reads are allowed, so not every future outer guard is context-only. Nothing is implemented or benchmarked. Compare approaches on the same goals: discover current admissible static destinations with safe labels, preserve source-owned authorization without copied policy, avoid rendering or unrelated list/result queries, keep an empty readable view available, recheck direct access and revocation, and distinguish unavailable checks from denial. A generated page descriptor can carry canonical owner/path, static localized caption and placement, and shared admission/render callables. Entry permission is not a promise that every later query/action succeeds.

discovery.instructions: Select the most coherent bounded discovery rule for this declared language.

criteria.derived_admission: Extract exact entry admission once and share it between sidebar discovery and request dispatch. Its work consists of inferred context prerequisites plus source page-level guards and only their necessary pure dependency reads; an unused data binding and all render-body queries/actions stay untouched. Guard-produced values remain server-private and can be passed to the active renderer under the same read checkpoint. Explicit denial excludes the link, while dependency or budget failure makes discovery unavailable. This honors dynamic page gates without adding source permissions, at the cost of relevant reads when authorization cannot be answered from context alone.
criteria.context_only_hidden: Permit automatic sidebar eligibility only when its required checks are statically context-only. For a page-level condition depending on business data, require existing nav=none and run the full guard solely on the requested route. Discovery then has a strict no-business-read bound, but valid destinations using data-sensitive gates lose automatic navigation unless their source changes.
criteria.candidate_links: Publish statically plausible destinations using context facts, leaving business-dependent conditions undecided until the selected page is requested. Direct dispatch remains fully authorized, and sidebar work uses no business reads. Some links will therefore lead to a denied page despite being listed; this deliberately weakens current-accessible navigation to candidate navigation.
